obligations.title: Add the duty: Set internal directives on structural foreign currency positions and have them approved by or notified to FINMA by bank category
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MarV-FINMA (SR 952.033.41), Art. 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Set internal directives on structural foreign currency positions and have them approved by or notified to FINMA by bank category

summaries.en: A bank's internal directives on structural foreign currency positions must settle at least which hedging positions may be exempted from the minimum capital, how the exempted amount is calculated, the tasks, powers, responsibilities, processes and internal reporting, how the positions are managed with adjustment frequency, limits and monitoring, and the measures that keep the exemption's conditions met. Banks of categories 1 and 2 need FINMA's approval of the directives and of every change before issuing them, banks of category 3 notify FINMA, and banks of categories 4 and 5 notify it on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep documented procedures for complete and correct trade data and reconcile every trade daily with the counterparty
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MarV-FINMA (SR 952.033.41), Art. 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Keep documented procedures for complete and correct trade data and reconcile every trade daily with the counterparty

summaries.en: A bank must have documented, internally reviewed and approved procedures, applied independently of the trading unit, ensuring that all transactions are recorded, valued and prepared for risk measurement completely, correctly and promptly, and that the data used in valuation models are complete, appropriate, consistent and current. Manual data corrections are documented so that their cause and exact content can be traced. Every transaction is reconciled daily with the counterparty, confirmations and reconciliation are done by a unit independent of trading, and discrepancies are cleared up with the counterparty without delay.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report changes to the market risk model approach and backtesting results to FINMA and the audit firm
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MarV-FINMA (SR 952.033.41), Art. 63, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report changes to the market risk model approach and backtesting results to FINMA and the audit firm

summaries.en: A bank using the market risk model approach must report to FINMA and its regulatory audit firm material changes to the approach, changes in its risk policy and in the structure and mandates of its trading desks, and the number of backtesting exceptions at bank level. At least every quarter it sends FINMA a report on the results of backtesting and of the profit and loss attribution tests at trading desk level and on the adjustment of the stress period.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have the risk monitoring system of the market risk model approach reviewed every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, MarV-FINMA (SR 952.033.41), Art. 64, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Have the risk monitoring system of the market risk model approach reviewed every year

summaries.en: Where a bank uses the market risk model approach, its internal audit or an audit firm licensed for regulatory audits must review every year the adequacy of its risk monitoring system, in particular the trading and control systems, under the Basel requirements the ordinance names. The review may be coordinated with the regulatory audit.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have the audit firm examine securitisations where the Basel standards call for supervisory consultation and inform FINMA of unusual ones
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KreV-FINMA (SR 952.033.21), Art. 58 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 5. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Have the audit firm examine securitisations where the Basel standards call for supervisory consultation and inform FINMA of unusual ones

summaries.en: Where the Basel minimum standards provide for consulting the supervisor on a securitisation, a bank must instruct its audit firm to examine it, and must also inform FINMA where the transaction is a novel securitisation, where it is not obvious that it is a securitisation, or where the bank uses separate loss allocation waterfalls for credit risk and dilution risk. This does not apply under the internal assessment approach for securitisations.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Handle margin agreements properly, cover collateral risks in risk management and keep collateral at custodians segregated
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KreV-FINMA (SR 952.033.21), Art. 83, consolidated German text, Stand am 5. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Handle margin agreements properly, cover collateral risks in risk management and keep collateral at custodians segregated

summaries.en: In securities financing transactions and other transactions secured by financial collateral, a bank must ensure that margin agreements with counterparties are handled properly. Its risk management covers the risks from margin agreements, concentrations in particular types of collateral, the reuse of collateral and rights assigned in collateral posted with the counterparty, and collateral deposited with a custodian is held separately from the custodian's own assets where possible.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check that the external ratings used are current and plausible and set the exemption criteria in an internal directive
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KreV-FINMA (SR 952.033.21), Art. 105, consolidated German text, Stand am 5. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Check that the external ratings used are current and plausible and set the exemption criteria in an internal directive

summaries.en: A bank using external ratings must check that they meet the eligibility requirements of the Capital Adequacy Ordinance and are current and plausible, judging plausibility by comparison with other available ratings and by evaluating financial news and market assessments of the credit risk of the position or counterparty. It sets in an internal directive the criteria by which immaterial positions are exempted from this due diligence.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report changes affecting the internal ratings based approach, get approval for material ones and send stress test results
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KreV-FINMA (SR 952.033.21), Art. 116 und Art. 118, consolidated German text, Stand am 5. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Report changes affecting the internal ratings based approach, get approval for material ones and send stress test results

summaries.en: A bank using the internal ratings based approach must report to FINMA and its audit firm every change in the facts behind its approval, in particular changes to the rating system or the risk practice, and must obtain FINMA's approval before continuing to use the approach where a change is material. It sends FINMA the results of its stress tests regularly.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Monitor exposures to central counterparties, report them to senior management and stress test clearing member obligations
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KreV-FINMA (SR 952.033.21), Art. 142, consolidated German text, Stand am 5. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Monitor exposures to central counterparties, report them to senior management and stress test clearing member obligations

summaries.en: A bank with exposures to a central counterparty must monitor them and inform senior management and the relevant committees of executive management and the board regularly about its trade exposures to each central counterparty and its obligations as a clearing member, such as default fund contributions and additional contribution duties. A clearing member also assesses the adequacy of its capital with scenario analyses and stress tests that include future claims and contingent liabilities from the default fund or from another clearing member's default or insolvency.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Lay down in directives how positions are allocated to the trading or banking book, control compliance and review it every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 2 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Lay down in directives how positions are allocated to the trading or banking book, control compliance and review it every year

summaries.en: A bank must have clearly defined principles and procedures, set out in directives that reflect its risk management capabilities, which ensure that positions are correctly allocated to the banking book or the trading book at the outset and when reclassified. Compliance with the directives is documented and continuously controlled and, where the regulatory audit does not cover it, reviewed every year by the internal audit, at a bank of category 4 or 5 that meets the de minimis conditions by another independent internal control body, or by a licensed audit firm.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Move no position between the trading and banking book except in extraordinary circumstances and with executive management's approval
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 4 Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 5 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Move no position between the trading and banking book except in extraordinary circumstances and with executive management's approval

summaries.en: A bank may not reclassify positions, a sale between the books included, from the trading book to the banking book or the reverse unless extraordinary circumstances exist, such as a change in accounting standards or giving up a trading activity; market events, changes in an instrument's liquidity or a change in holding intent do not count. Each reclassification needs the approval of executive management, which may delegate it under rules and escalation procedures set in the internal directives.

payload.refLabel: Art. 4 Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 5 Abs. 1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Document each deviating initial allocation and reclassification and submit the directives on them to FINMA by bank category
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Document each deviating initial allocation and reclassification and submit the directives on them to FINMA by bank category

summaries.en: A bank must document individually every initial allocation that deviates from the rules and every reclassification, and lay down principles and procedures for both in directives that meet the requirements for the book allocation directives. Banks of categories 1 and 2 need FINMA's approval of these directives and of every change before issuing them, banks of category 3 notify FINMA, and banks of categories 4 and 5 notify it on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report deviating allocations and reclassifications every quarter or year and submit the report to FINMA
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Report deviating allocations and reclassifications every quarter or year and submit the report to FINMA

summaries.en: A bank must record every deviating initial allocation and every reclassification in a report giving in particular its date, materiality, instrument and reasons, and showing whether a reclassification reduced the minimum capital when it was made and how the capital surcharge was calculated. Banks of categories 1 and 2 prepare the report every quarter and banks of categories 3 to 5 every year, and banks of categories 1 to 3 submit it to FINMA.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run a prudent valuation process with written procedures, an independent valuation unit and monthly price verification
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 17 und Art. 23, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Run a prudent valuation process with written procedures, an independent valuation unit and monthly price verification

summaries.en: A bank must be able to value its positions prudently and reliably also under stress and to use alternative methods when market prices or inputs are no longer available. It sets out in directives and documented procedures how valuation fits into risk management, how the need for valuation adjustments is assessed and the adjustments calculated and continuously reviewed, how prices and inputs are verified independently of trading, the responsibilities, data sources, use of unobservable inputs, valuation frequency, closing price times and reconciliation procedures. The valuation unit is independent of trading, checks market and model based valuations at least monthly and reports up to executive management.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Contact FINMA without delay when US GAAP or the bank's procedures for applying it change
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, HBEV-FINMA (SR 952.031.11), Art. 55, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2025

titles.en: Contact FINMA without delay when US GAAP or the bank's procedures for applying it change

summaries.en: A bank that applies US GAAP must contact FINMA without delay when the standard or its internal procedures for applying it change, and give FINMA information on the valuation principles it applies to financial instruments.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report changes in the registration facts at once and confirm every year that the intermediaries' registration facts are true
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO-FINMA (SR 961.011.1), Art. 91, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Report changes in the registration facts at once and confirm every year that the intermediaries' registration facts are true

summaries.en: A registered insurance intermediary must report to FINMA, promptly after learning of it, every change in the facts behind its registration, in particular in the details and documents listed in Annex 6 of the Supervision Ordinance and the further details given for the register. The persons entrusted with management or administration confirm to FINMA every year that the registration facts of the intermediaries who arrange insurance business for them are true and up to date.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Prepare a yearly report on key figures for FINMA as at 31 December and file it by 31 May
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO-FINMA (SR 961.011.1), Art. 93, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Prepare a yearly report on key figures for FINMA as at 31 December and file it by 31 May

summaries.en: A registered insurance intermediary must prepare every year, as at 31 December, a report for FINMA on the key figures and information about its activity that supervision needs, as FINMA defines and publishes them by 30 September for the following year. It submits the report on the past business year by 31 May of the next year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Base example calculations for non-qualified life insurance on three return scenarios and show the costs in the middle one
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AVO-FINMA (SR 961.011.1), Art. 86 und Art. 87 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Base example calculations for non-qualified life insurance on three return scenarios and show the costs in the middle one

summaries.en: An insurer's example calculations for non-qualified life insurance must use at least a favourable, a middle and an unfavourable return scenario over the contract term, point to favourable and unfavourable cases in a balanced way and illustrate the chances and risks of profit participation, resting on current surpluses in the middle scenario where their financing is plausible over the whole term. The insurer checks and documents internally that the calculations can be financed in every scenario, and shows in the middle scenario the gross tariff return, the return reduction, the net return, the risk costs and any separate premiums for supplementary insurance. For contracts in class A2 the Supervision Ordinance's rules for qualified life insurance apply instead.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell FINMA without delay of the choice and of every change of audit firm
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMA-PV (SR 956.161), Art. 13 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2015

titles.en: Tell FINMA without delay of the choice and of every change of audit firm

summaries.en: A supervised firm must notify FINMA without delay when it chooses an audit firm and whenever it changes it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint the same audit firm, or one of its network, for every supervised firm of the group
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMA-PV (SR 956.161), Art. 13 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2015

titles.en: Appoint the same audit firm, or one of its network, for every supervised firm of the group

summaries.en: All supervised firms that belong to the same group or conglomerate must appoint for the audit the same audit firm or an audit firm of the same network. FINMA may allow exceptions in justified cases.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the audit firm the internal audit's reports in good time
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMA-PV (SR 956.161), Art. 13 Abs. 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2015

titles.en: Give the audit firm the internal audit's reports in good time

summaries.en: A supervised firm must send its audit firm the reports of its internal audit in good time.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Agree no flat fee and no fixed time budget for an audit mandate
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMA-PV (SR 956.161), Art. 8 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2015

titles.en: Agree no flat fee and no fixed time budget for an audit mandate

summaries.en: An audit mandate under the ordinance may not be paid by a flat fee, and in particular no set amount of time may be agreed for it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Obtain the listed identification details of each beneficial owner and report them with the control details to the register
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPV (SR 955.31), Art. 10 und Art. 20 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Obtain the listed identification details of each beneficial owner and report them with the control details to the register

summaries.en: A legal entity that must identify a natural person obtains the name and first names, date of birth, nationalities and municipality, postcode and state of residence, and checks whether the person has a Swiss social security (AHV) number, obtaining a copy of a passport, identity card or Swiss foreigner's identity card where there is none. It reports to the transparency register for each beneficial owner these details and the information on the kind and extent of control and the chain of control, and, where it reports the most senior member of its managing body in the alternative, that person's function.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report what is known and a contact person where a beneficial owner cannot be identified or verified
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPV (SR 955.31), Art. 21, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Report what is known and a contact person where a beneficial owner cannot be identified or verified

summaries.en: Where a legal entity fails to identify a beneficial owner or to verify the identity or status of one, it reports the relevant information it holds, including on the chain of control and on shareholders or partners who did not meet their duty to report, and the identification details and function of the most senior member of its managing body as contact person. Where it could verify only some of several beneficial owners, it reports the full details for those and this information for the others.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Query the transparency register only for anti-money laundering due diligence and clarify suspected misuse when told of it
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPV (SR 955.31), Art. 54 Abs. 2 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Query the transparency register only for anti-money laundering due diligence and clarify suspected misuse when told of it

summaries.en: A financial intermediary's users may query the transparency register only in direct connection with its due diligence duties under the Anti-Money Laundering Act; frequent, unusual or repeated queries on the same person or entity can point to misuse. When the registry authority informs the financial intermediary of suspected misuse by one of its users, it must make the necessary clarifications and tell the authority the result.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give a discrepancy report the date, the author, the entity, the discrepancy and its grounds
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPV (SR 955.31), Art. 55 Abs. 1 und 2, Art. 56 und Art. 57, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Give a discrepancy report the date, the author, the entity, the discrepancy and its grounds

summaries.en: A financial intermediary reporting a discrepancy to the transparency register must give at least the date, itself as author, the name, seat and enterprise identification number (UID) of the legal entity and the information concerned or the missing entry, with one or more of the grounds the ordinance lists, such as an identified beneficial owner who is not registered or wrongly registered control. Discrepancies that stem from the differing anti-money laundering rules, raise no doubt about the beneficial owner information, concern only the chain of control without raising such doubt, or arise before an entry deadline has passed need not be reported. The reporting deadline starts when the client's period to clarify has passed unused or its answer does not resolve the discrepancy.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Treat an attack as reportable when it disrupts systems, forces emergency plans, exposes business information, went undetected for 90 days or involves extortion
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, CSV (SR 128.51), Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Treat an attack as reportable when it disrupts systems, forces emergency plans, exposes business information, went undetected for 90 days or involves extortion

summaries.en: For the duty to report cyberattacks, the functioning of a critical infrastructure counts as endangered when staff or third parties are affected by system outages or the organisation can keep up its activities only with emergency plans. Information counts as manipulated or leaked when unauthorised persons have seen, changed or disclosed business information or a data security breach was notified under the Data Protection Act, an attack counts as long undetected when it happened more than 90 days before, and it counts as linked to extortion, threats or coercion when these target the reporting organisation or people working for it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give in a cyberattack report when the attack happened and was found, the attacker, any extortion and the attack's effects
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, CSV (SR 128.51), Art. 15, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Give in a cyberattack report when the attack happened and was found, the attacker, any extortion and the attack's effects

summaries.en: Beside the details the Information Security Act requires, a cyberattack report must give the date and time the attack was detected and took place, information on the attacker, whether extortion, threats or coercion were involved and whether a criminal complaint was filed, and the severity of the impact on the availability, integrity and confidentiality of information and on the organisation's ability to function. A report not made through the Federal Office for Cybersecurity's communication system also gives the organisation's name and address and the reporting person's contact details.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Complete an incomplete cyberattack report within the 14 days the Federal Office for Cybersecurity grants
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, CSV (SR 128.51), Art. 16, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Complete an incomplete cyberattack report within the 14 days the Federal Office for Cybersecurity grants

summaries.en: Where not all required information is known within the 24 hours allowed for the report, the organisation completes it within the 14 days the Federal Office for Cybersecurity grants. If information is still missing when that period ends, it must at the Office's request complete the report at once or confirm that the information does not exist.

obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Syrien-Verordnung (SR 196.127.27), Art. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 31. Juli 2025

titles.en: Freeze the funds and economic resources of the persons listed under the Guatemala ordinance

summaries.en: Under the Guatemala ordinance, funds and economic resources owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by the persons, companies and organisations listed in the Annex, by those acting on their behalf or at their direction, and by companies and organisations they own or control are frozen. Interest and other income on frozen accounts, payments under existing contracts or under arbitral awards or court or authority decisions given or enforceable in Switzerland, the EEA or the United Kingdom, and funds that third parties transfer to a listed person may be credited to frozen accounts only if the amounts credited are frozen as well. SECO may allow payments from frozen accounts or releases of frozen assets in the exceptional cases the ordinance lists.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Make no funds or economic resources available to the persons listed under the Guatemala ordinance
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über Massnahmen betreffend Guatemala (SR 946.231.137.6), Art. 2 Abs. 2 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 27. Januar 2026

titles.en: Make no funds or economic resources available to the persons listed under the Guatemala ordinance

summaries.en: It is prohibited to transfer funds to the persons, companies and organisations whose assets the Guatemala ordinance freezes, or to make funds or economic resources available to them in any other way, directly or indirectly. The prohibition does not apply where a transfer is needed for humanitarian activities or other activities meeting basic human needs by the United Nations, international and humanitarian organisations and the other bodies the ordinance names.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Satisfy no claims of the persons the Guatemala ordinance names on transactions the measures blocked
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über Massnahmen betreffend Guatemala (SR 946.231.137.6), Art. 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 27. Januar 2026

titles.en: Satisfy no claims of the persons the Guatemala ordinance names on transactions the measures blocked

summaries.en: It is prohibited to satisfy claims of the persons, companies and organisations listed in the Annex or of those acting on their behalf, where the claim goes back to a contract or transaction whose performance the measures of the Guatemala ordinance prevented or impaired, directly or indirectly. In proceedings to enforce such a claim, the claimant must prove that satisfying it is not prohibited.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report assets caught by the Guatemala freeze to SECO without delay
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Verordnung über Massnahmen betreffend Guatemala (SR 946.231.137.6), Art. 6, consolidated German text, Stand am 27. Januar 2026

titles.en: Report assets caught by the Guatemala freeze to SECO without delay

summaries.en: Anyone who holds or manages funds, or knows of funds or economic resources, that must be assumed to fall under the Guatemala freeze must report them to SECO without delay, with the beneficiaries' names and the subject and value of the frozen assets; credits of third-party transfers to frozen accounts are reported without delay with the names of the senders. A financial institution that has reported funds it holds or manages sends SECO every year by 15 February the amounts as at 31 December of the previous year.
